close_reason: Implemented option (a) from the bead: pinned the matching strategy in the issuer_dn_contains constructor rustdoc and added a multi-RDN regression test using the PKITS GoodCACert fixture (CN=Trust Anchor,O=Test Certificates 2011,C=US — the only multi-RDN issuer in workspace fixtures). The test asserts the rendered DN as an independent oracle and exercises four positive substring patterns plus three negative ones (space-after-comma, C-first reordering, long attribute name). Documentation now explicitly warns against multi-RDN substrings spanning the renderer's comma separator and recommends single-RDN-value patterns; the renderer-version-coupling hazard is documented as a known caveat. Commit landing.
description:
deviation.rs:608-625 (DeviationScope::matches for SCOPE_KIND_ISSUER_DN_CONTAINS): substring match runs against cert.tbs_certificate.issuer.to_string().to_lowercase(). The .to_string() of a Name is RFC 4514 rendering — comma-separated, RDN-ordered, attribute-type prefixes included.

Failure mode: an operator writes 'issuer_dn_contains: agency-x ca' expecting to match a cert whose CN is 'Agency-X CA'. RFC 4514 rendering produces something like 'CN=Agency-X CA,O=Department of X,C=US'. The lowercase comparison against 'agency-x ca' works (no commas in the substring), but extending to 'agency-x ca, department' breaks because the actual rendering may use different separator whitespace, attribute order, or escape characters. In particular RFC 4514 mandates RDN reversal — the operator who writes 'agency-x ca,o=department' expecting CN-first ordering will silently miss certs whose Name encoder reverses RDNs.

Worse: cert.tbs_certificate.issuer.to_string() depends on x509-cert's RFC 4514 implementation. Any change there (escaping rules, ordering, attribute display name) silently changes which certs match without any version bump in pkix-lint.

Maintainer consequence: this is a class of 'why doesn't my deviation match' tickets. The fix is to either (a) document the matching strategy precisely (cert.to_string() RFC 4514 form, lowercase, substring-only) and warn against multi-RDN patterns; or (b) switch the matcher to a per-RDN scan (iterate RDNs, lowercase each attribute value, check substring) which is more predictable but doesn't allow cross-RDN patterns. The current shape is the worst of both — operators write patterns that look like they should work and silently don't.

Pin the strategy. Document it on the constructor. Add a regression test with a multi-RDN issuer showing what does and doesn't match.
title: DeviationScope::issuer_dn_contains substring matches on Name::to_string output not on RDN values
